title: Tiered segmentation for per-customer batching & caching automation
creator: Maya Hernandez
description: Deliver an automated policy layer that recommends and safely applies batching and KV/ prefix caching configurations per-customer and per-route. Policies are driven by customer segmentation and tier (free/dev/prod/enterprise), with allowlist/denylist overrides and a safe apply/rollback workflow (canary, staged rollout, automatic rollback on SLO regressions). The feature must produce actionable recommendations (batch size, batching window, cache TTL, KV reuse thresholds), a confidence score, and a one-click apply that respects guardrails and audit requirements.
acceptance_criteria: Recommend per-route batching and caching parameters for at least 80% of sampled customer workloads with a confidence score and justification.
Support segmentation rules: by customer tier, explicit allowlist/denylist, and per-route labels.
Provide safe-apply path: canary rollout to 5% traffic, realtime SLO monitoring (latency and error), and automatic rollback if latency or error increase exceeds thresholds within observation window.
Produce audit trail (who applied what, when) and integrate with KMS-backed config store for Private deployments.
Expose recommendations and rollout controls in Console (API + UI) and emit metrics to our observability pipeline (per-route token cost delta, latency change, cache hit rate change).
implementation_notes: Policy engine will evaluate historical traffic slices (7-day window) to produce per-route request size distribution and cold start/kv-hit characteristics.
Recommendation algorithm: cost-savings heuristic + latency-safety penalty -> objective score. Recommend several candidates (aggressive/moderate/conservative) with estimated token savings.
Safe apply uses staged routing via smart routing layer: start with route percentage, measure tail latency (p99), median latency, and error rate. Thresholds configurable per-customer tier.
Allowlist/denylist model: allow explicit customer IDs and route regex; denylist prevents any automated apply and surfaces guidance only.
Data retention: store inputs to recommendations for 30 days for repro and evals; mask PII keys before storage for enterprise customers.

Trade-offs: aggressive batching increases throughput and reduces cost but may raise tail latency for low-concurrency routes. We'll bias conservative defaults for free/dev tiers and allow higher aggressiveness for enterprise tiers with SLA opt-in.
